newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey calls for end to Middle East bloodshed.
newsitem.headline: Turkey calls for end to Middle East bloodshed.

text.p: Turkey called on Monday for reason to prevail between Israel and the Palestinians after clashes last week in which some 70 people died.

"The loss of life, the shooting against the Palestinian demonstratiors are most disturbing. We are hoping that again reason will prevail in the area and the parties will find a way to stop that bloodshed," foreign ministry spokesman Sermet Atacanli told a news conference.
At least 55 Palestinians and 14 Israelis have been killed in the clashes that erupted over Israel's decision to open a tunnel near Jerusalem's al-Aqsa mosque, Islam's third holiest shrine.
Under pressure from Turkey's influential military, Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan has backtracked on promises to scrap a military training accord signed with Israel in February.
Turkey also signed a defence industry deal with the Jewish state in August.
U.S. President Bill Clinton has invited Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat to visit Washington this week to try to end the Middle East violence.
Arafat has asked for a delay in the summit, scheduled for Tuesday, until differences over the agenda are settled.
